- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for 30d horizon.
- Model consistently underestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for 30d horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias — if 30d forecast is flat or trending downward, true outcome often reverses upward; add 1–3% upward bias if recent 7d average is falling.
- For 30d forecasts, if model is trending upward with no sentiment signal, reduce slope by 10–20% to avoid over-optimism.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.0 values with no recent spike, model often fails to capture volatility; add 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast range.
